`Vector3.project(camera)` is implemented in `math/Vector3.js` at lines 499–503. It works by chaining two `applyMatrix4` calls:

```js
project( camera ) {
    return this.applyMatrix4( camera.matrixWorldInverse ).applyMatrix4( camera.projectionMatrix );
}
```

**The two camera matrices applied:**
1. `camera.matrixWorldInverse` — the inverse of the camera's world matrix (the view matrix), which transforms the vector from world space into camera space.
2. `camera.projectionMatrix` — the camera's projection matrix, which transforms from camera space into normalized device coordinate (NDC) space.

**Order of application:** The matrices are applied in sequence via the chained `applyMatrix4` calls. First `camera.matrixWorldInverse` is applied (world space → camera space), then `camera.projectionMatrix` is applied (camera space → NDC space). This matches the method's purpose of projecting a vector from world space into the camera's NDC space.

For reference, the inverse operation `unproject(camera)` (lines 512–516) reverses this by applying `camera.projectionMatrixInverse` first, then `camera.matrixWorld`.

**Tracking mechanism:** `LoadingManager` (defined in `loaders/LoadingManager.js`, class at lines 18–324) tracks in-flight loads with a simple counter-based approach via closure variables set in the constructor (lines 31–35):

- `isLoading` — boolean, true while any item is in flight
- `itemsLoaded` — count of completed items
- `itemsTotal` — count of items started

It does **not** track per-URL in-flight state; progress is purely counter-based.

**Lifecycle functions:**

- **Load starts** — `itemStart(url)` (lines 86–102): increments `itemsTotal`, invokes `this.onStart(url, itemsLoaded, itemsTotal)` if no load is in progress, then sets `isLoading = true`.
- **Load finishes** — `itemEnd(url)` (lines 110–132): increments `itemsLoaded`, invokes `this.onProgress(url, itemsLoaded, itemsTotal)`, and when `itemsLoaded === itemsTotal` sets `isLoading = false` and invokes `this.onLoad()`.
- **Load errors** — `itemError(url)` (lines 140–148): invokes `this.onError(url)` only; it does **not** adjust the counters, so an errored item never triggers the completion condition.

The `onStart`/`onLoad`/`onProgress`/`onError` callbacks are registered in the constructor (lines 46–70).

`BatchedMesh.raycast()` (objects/BatchedMesh.js, lines 1384–1442) does not create a new mesh per geometry. It reuses a module-level singleton `_mesh = new Mesh()` (line 90) along with a shared scratch array `_batchIntersects = []` (line 91).

For each geometry in the batch, it copies the following onto that reused `_mesh`:

1. **Before the loop** (lines 1392–1405):
   - `_mesh.material = this.material` (line 1392)
   - `_mesh.geometry.index = batchGeometry.index` (line 1393)
   - `_mesh.geometry.attributes = batchGeometry.attributes` (line 1394)
   - `_mesh.geometry.boundingBox` / `boundingSphere` are lazily initialized to `new Box3()` / `new Sphere()` if null (lines 1395–1405)

2. **Per-geometry inside the loop** (lines 1417–1422):
   - `_mesh.geometry.setDrawRange(geometryInfo.start, geometryInfo.count)` (line 1417) — selects the vertex/index slice belonging to that geometry
   - `_mesh.matrixWorld` — the instance's local matrix is fetched via `this.getMatrixAt(i, _mesh.matrixWorld)` then `.premultiply(matrixWorld)` to produce the full world transform (line 1420)
   - `_mesh.geometry.boundingBox` — filled via `this.getBoundingBoxAt(geometryId, ...)` (line 1421)

The ray is not copied at all — the incoming `raycaster` is passed straight through to `_mesh.raycast(raycaster, _batchIntersects)` (line 1423).

In `renderers/common/Animation.js`, the `start()` method (lines 69–99) defines a recursive `update` callback (line 71). Inside `update`, the next frame is scheduled by calling `this._context.requestAnimationFrame( update )` (line 73), where `this._context` is `self`/`window` (line 45). The callback is kicked off once by calling `update()` directly (line 97). Each frame it also invokes the user-defined animation loop callback `this._animationLoop( time, xrFrame )` if one is set (lines 89–92). The loop is stopped via `stop()`, which calls `this._context.cancelAnimationFrame( this._requestId )` (line 108).

The handle is stored in the instance attribute `this._requestId` (declared lines 55–62, assigned at line 73, reset to `null` at line 110). This is the handle used to cancel the loop.
